The mass of the filament is estimated by equating the electrical energy supplied over half a cycle to the heat required to raise the filament's temperature from 3000 °C to 3200 °C. For an AC circuit, the instantaneous power varies as \(P(t) = P_{\text{max}} \sin^2(\omega_0 t)\), where the temperature fluctuation occurs at angular frequency \(\omega = 2\omega_0\). Over the half‑cycle when the temperature rises (\(\Delta t = \pi/\omega\)), the energy input is \(\pi P_{\text{max}}/(2\omega)\). This energy equals \(m c (T_1 - T_0)\). Solving for mass gives  
\[
m = \frac{\pi P_{\text{max}}}{2\,\omega\,c\,(T_1 - T_0)}.
\]  
Substituting \(P_{\text{max}} = 10\ \text{W}\), \(\omega = 0.02\ \text{s}^{-1}\), \(c = 235\ \text{J/(K·kg)}\), and \(T_1 - T_0 = 200\ \text{K}\) yields \(m \approx 0.0167\ \text{kg}\).

ANSWER: 0.0167 kg
